memos.risk:
Risk view on POTS: the coin is alive and organic-classed, but several signals are weak. Bundle share is 38% of the curve, a launch bot was present, and sell-to-buy in the first two minutes was 0.95, so early flippers were heavy. Pool depth is 96 SOL, adequate for a $20 ticket (roughly 0.1 SOL, about 2% of pool), so impact is manageable.

If the desk buys: ticket $5 (the low end, given bundling and the 22% drawdown from the 30-minute high). Stop at 25%. Hold 15-30 minutes, then exit regardless.

Refuse any size if: bundle share rises further or the top-3 concentration moves up, net flow turns negative for a sustained window, the drawdown deepens past 30% (stop out instead), or the pool thins below roughly 60 SOL. Given the base rates, I'd lean toward skipping unless the desk is comfortable with a small, time-boxed bet.
memos.scout:
Case for buying POTS now is thin, and I'd lean toward skipping.

The strongest points: the coin is classed ORGANIC, not a factory or operator-backed launch, with no airdrop dump seen. Buyers are broad (407 buyers in the last 15 minutes, 452 on the curve, top-3 holder share about 7%), and it is up 26.6% over 30 minutes and 133% over the last 15, with net positive flow of 37.7 SOL.

Against that: the last-15-minute flow is only about 60% of volume cleared on the buy side and sellers (310) nearly match buyers in count, sell-to-buy in the first two minutes after graduation was 0.95, and it is already 22% off its 30-minute high. The bundle share of 38% is a warning sign. A launch bot was present, and a $20 entry plus a 1.4-5.1% round trip means we need a move well above fees to profit. Nothing here shows demand that will hold for the next 30-60 minutes, and the base rate for this setup is a loss.

Recommendation: skip.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: insider distribution into the post-graduation bid. The 38% bundle share on the curve and the launch bot present at graduation point to coordinated early wallets. Those wallets are already sitting on a 1.33x last-15-minute run and a 22% drawdown from the 30-minute high, with sell SOL (175.65) running at about 82% of buy SOL (213.35) in the last window. Net flow is only +37.7 SOL on $45k volume, so the bid is thin and most of the buying is churn. The first two minutes show a 0.95 sell-to-buy ratio, which means early holders were already exiting. With only 96 SOL of pool depth, a $20 round trip costing 1.4-5.1% plus impact leaves little room for a modest move to pay. Skip.
